newsitem.title: USA: More strep deaths reported in New York state.
newsitem.headline: More strep deaths reported in New York state.

text.p: Medical authorities in Rochester, where a woman died last week of a rare "flesh-eating" bacteria, have announced the death of two more people from the strep infection that can cause the disease.
Announcement of the two deaths late on Tuesday brought to four the number of people known to have died this year as a result of invasive group A streptococcus infections, health officials said.

Monroe County health officials said only two of 19 people infected so far this year in the county, which includes Rochester, contracted necrotizing fascitis, the "flesh-eating" form. One died on Friday and the other is recovering.

The two most recent deaths were women who were patients at Strong Memorial Hospital in Rochester, the same hospital where 39-year-old Susan Dougherty died on Friday. One woman died in January and the other in February, officials said. Their names were not immediately released.
Dougherty had a baby by Caesarean section at the hospital in February and the bacteria started in her surgical wound, sources said.

"We have every reason to believe that the cluster of three cases among obstetrical patients is over and that it is entirely safe for patients to deliver babies or have surgery or whatever treatment they seek here at Strong Memorial," Paul Gramm, an infectious disease specialist at the hospital, said.

In nearby Ontario County, a rural area outside Rochester, a 10-year-old boy died from pneumonia associated with the Group A streptococcus, but he did not have the "flesh-eating" bacteria, authorities said.

There are 10,000 to 15,000 cases of invasive group strep annually in the United States, the federal Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, says. About one in 10 progresses to necrotizing fascitis and death rates from this strain range from 20 percent to 60 percent, the CDC says.
